newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan court grants bail to ex-trader Hamanaka--Kyodo.
newsitem.headline: Japan court grants bail to ex-trader Hamanaka--Kyodo.

text.p: A Japanese court on Monday approved the release of former copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka on bail of 50 million yen ($409,000), Kyodo news agency reported.

Hamanaka, 49, arrested last October on suspicion of defrauding his former company, Sumitomo Corp, with unauthorised trades that created losses of $2.6 billion, pleaded guilty to fraud and forgery charges at the start of his trial last week.
A Tokyo District Court spokesman said he was unable to confirm the report, adding that all information about bail is confidential.
Hamanaka had requested bail last autumn before his trial started, but the request was refused.
The reported move comes in the middle of Hamanaka's trial on fraud and forgery charges, which had its first hearing a week ago.

At that session, Hamanaka admitted the charges, which relate to improper trades that cost his former employer $2.6 billion. The trial continues on March 10, with the defence planning to introduce evidence showing mitigating circumstances for his actions. ($1=122 yen)
